what: Seagate makes hard disk drives. Its drives store the bulk of the world's data in cloud data centres, where capacity per dollar matters more than speed. New HAMR technology lets it put far more data on each disk.
customers: Cloud and hyperscale data centre operators first, then enterprises and consumer electronics makers.
money: high-capacity nearline drives for cloud and enterprise storage
drives and systems for edge, video surveillance and consumer use
moat: Only two companies still make hard drives at scale, with factories and head technology that would take years and billions to recreate.
risks: Hard drive demand has historically been deeply cyclical, with sharp down years
Flash memory keeps taking share in applications where speed matters
A few cloud customers make up much of demand
HAMR production has to ramp cleanly to keep its cost advantage
opportunities: AI data centres need enormous low-cost capacity, which is exactly what hard drives provide
Only two suppliers means pricing has held up unusually well in this cycle
HAMR drives raise capacity per unit, which lifts both revenue and margin
watch: Exabytes shipped and average price per terabyte, and how fast HAMR drives reach volume.
